title: Nonequilibrium dynamics of doped Chern ferromagnets: a case study for false vacuum decay
authors: Kilian Kuhlbrodt, Olivier Huber, Oliver Breach, Weijie Li, Xiaodong Xu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Martin Kroner, Siddharth A. Parameswaran, Atac Imamoglu
abstract: Even though metastable false vacuum decay is ubiquitous in physics, its underlying dynamics are still not well understood. Dissipative state preparation in moiré quantum materials provides an exceptional setting for exploring this physics since it allows the possibility of generating exotic quantum states that are not the ground state of the system Hamiltonian. Motivated by recent experiments demonstrating steady-state optical orientation of the spin-valley degree of freedom of holes, here we investigate dynamics of itinerant and Chern ferromagnets in the presence of an opposing magnetic field. Optical pumping using a circularly polarized Laguerre-Gauss beam allows us to deterministically prepare a true vacuum bubble embedded inside a metastable state. Depending on its initial size controlled by the pump power, we observe that the bubble collapses or expands due to an interplay between domain wall and bulk dynamics. For external magnetic fields comparable to the coercive field of ferromagnetism, we observe up to two-orders-of-magnitude prolongation of the spin polarization decay time at commensurate fillings corresponding to integer and fractional Chern insulator states. Our experiments reveal that the nonequilibrium dynamics of the ferromagnetic domains is substantially more sensitive to the precise filling factor around Chern insulator states than standard transport or optical measurements.
summary: This experimental work explores false vacuum decay in doped Chern ferromagnets using moiré quantum materials. By optically creating and monitoring expanding/collapsing 'vacuum bubbles,' the authors show that the decay rate is extremely sensitive to doping levels near topological insulator fillings. This highlights how correlated electron physics, governed by topology, dictates non-equilibrium stability.
main_problem: The study investigates the underlying dynamics of metastable false vacuum decay, a process relevant across physics from cosmology to magnetism.
main_result: False vacuum decay is dramatically slowed down at commensurate filling factors near Chern insulator states when external magnetic fields are comparable to the coercive field. The decay dynamics are highly sensitive to the precise doping level around these topological states.
method: The researchers employed an optical pump-probe scheme using circularly polarized Laguerre-Gauss beams to deterministically create and monitor a true vacuum bubble embedded within a metastable ferromagnetic state.
model_or_system: The system is realized in doped Chern ferromagnets, specifically utilizing twisted molybdenum ditelluride (t-MoTe2) moiré quantum materials. These materials exhibit spin-valley polarized Stoner-like ferromagnetic states with non-zero Chern numbers.

why_interesting: The connection between topological invariants (Chern numbers) and non-equilibrium dynamics like vacuum decay provides a rich playground for open quantum systems theory, suggesting that topology can stabilize or destabilize metastable states in engineered solid-state platforms.
